questions.q: Why are dashboards a service-only feature?
options: Dashboards can't be built or viewed inside Power BI Desktop at all — they exist only in the Power BI service
Dashboards can be built in Desktop but not viewed in the service
Dashboards are actually available in Desktop, just under a different name
Dashboards only exist on mobile devices
questions.explain: Unlike reports, dashboards are never built or displayed in Desktop. You can view and share existing dashboards on mobile, but you can't create one there either.

questions.q: What is a 'tile' on a Power BI dashboard?
options: One visualization pinned onto the dashboard, most often from a report page
The dashboard's background color scheme
A separate license type
A synonym for an entire semantic model
questions.explain: Tiles are the individual visualizations that make up a dashboard. You pin them from a report, another dashboard, Excel, or a Q&A result.

questions.q: How many semantic models can a single dashboard combine tiles from?
options: One or more — unlike a report, which is always based on exactly one semantic model
Always exactly one, same as a report
Dashboards never connect to any semantic model
A maximum of two, no more
questions.explain: A dashboard can pull tiles from several different reports and semantic models into one consolidated view — something a single report page, tied to one semantic model, can't do.

questions.q: Can you filter or slice a Power BI dashboard the way you can a report?
options: No — dashboards can't be filtered or sliced; that level of interaction belongs to the report a tile links to
Yes, dashboards support every filter and slicer a report does
Only if the dashboard has fewer than five tiles
Only on mobile devices
questions.explain: Dashboards are meant to be glanced at, not interacted with like a report. Filtering and slicing happen in the underlying report — clicking a tile takes you there.

questions.q: What license or permission is required to create a dashboard in a shared workspace?
options: Edit permissions on the underlying report, which generally requires a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User license
No license is ever required to create a dashboard anywhere
Only a Fabric admin can ever create a dashboard
A Free license is sufficient in every workspace
questions.explain: Creating a dashboard needs edit permissions on the report being pinned from — in a shared workspace that requires Pro or PPU, though My Workspace allows it without either.
